2015_074_011315mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education packet for the Annual Organizational and Regular Meeting of January 13, 2015 pairs the year's organizational business — officer elections, appointment of Rick L. West as Treasurer, the depository and investment resolution, and the 2015 meeting calendar — with the November 2014 Treasurer's Report and its full check, ACH, wire transfer and P-Card registers. Total disbursements in the period were $8,040,586.63, of which $5,979,045.87 were check disbursements. Also carried are Schools of Choice Section 105 and 105c resolutions for 2015-16, a Superintendent Goals update, and a Barton Malow bond construction update.

**Meeting**
Annual Organizational and Regular Meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, Tuesday, January 13, 2015, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000), cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Roll-call rosters list seven trustees: Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood.

**Organizational actions**
Judy Holmes named temporary secretary and designated to post meeting notices; President, Vice President and Secretary elected to serve until December 31, 2015, four votes required. Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed nonvoting Treasurer for January through December 2015. The Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution names twelve institutions, including Bank of America, JP Morgan Chase, Comerica, Fifth Third, Flagstar Bancorp, PNC and MILAF managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc.; investments follow Board Policy D-1103, with fund combination authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. continue as legal counsel for 2015; Superintendent Richard M. Machesky continues as Deputy Secretary.

**December 2, 2014 minutes (consent item)**
Resolutions 14-117 through 14-124 each carried 7-0: acceptance of the audit for the year ended June 30, 2014 presented by Plante Moran partner Teresa Pollock; appointment of Rick West as December 2014 Treasurer; MAISL Joint Risk Management Trust designations of West and Patricia Orczykowski; authorization to consider refunding the 2006 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds dated May 24, 2006, with estimated savings of $3,356,520; rescission of the Integrated Design Solutions, LLC award and approval of Convergent/Wright & Hunter; and a Gorno Ford fleet vehicle award of $28,479.00 under MiDEAL contract #071B1300005. Bemis and Wattles Elementary were recognized among 337 National Blue Ribbon Schools.

2015_074_011315mtg.verbose:
**Meeting identity.** The Troy Board of Education held its Annual Organizational and Regular Meeting at 7:00 PM on Tuesday, January 13, 2015 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000 (www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools; the packet ends at page 164.

**Organizational items.** Superintendent Richard M. Machesky's agenda memo sets out election of an acting chairperson, appointment of Judy Holmes as temporary secretary, and election of President, Vice President and Secretary, each serving until December 31, 2015, with four votes required for election. Roll-call rosters name the seven members: Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood. Item 4.B appoints Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as nonvoting Treasurer of the Board for January through December 2015. Item 4.C adopts the Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution for the same period, designating twelve institutions: Bank of America, Bank of New York, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, First Merit Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus) managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Checks carry the facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West, with emergency handwritten authority for the Treasurer or Superintendent Machesky on the Bank of America General Fund and Payroll accounts; PNC Bank accounts pay Troy Career Center expenses and a Comerica Bank account pays flexible spending claims by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc. Investments are made under Board Policy D-1103, and the Treasurer may combine money from more than one fund for investments authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code; certification is by the Secretary, Oakland County, Michigan, this 13th day of January 2015. Items 4.D through 4.F continue Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. as legal counsel for calendar 2015, the Superintendent as Deputy Secretary, and Judy Holmes as the person posting meeting notices. Item 4.G adopts the calendar of Tuesday regular meetings on January 13, February 3, March 3, April 14, May 5, June 2 (at Athens), June 16, July 7, August 4, September 1, October 6, November 10 and December 1, 2015, with the next organizational meeting January 12, 2016, plus 6:00 PM workshops through the year and a Winter Retreat on Saturday, January 24, 2015 at 9:30 AM.

**Recognitions.** January is Board of Education Recognition Month, marked with a CD of district music. The TSD Mission Moment features the Athens High School urban farming initiative, a Pingree 4-H program led by teacher Christina Harlan joining Athens High School and Baker and Larson Middle School students at a Detroit farm, showing animals at the Oakland County Fair. Bemis Elementary Principal Jeremey Whan was named Outstanding Practicing Principal by the Michigan Elementary and Middle School Principals Association, introduced by MEMSPA Executive Director Paul Liabenow.

**December 2, 2014 minutes.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 PM with all seven members present and approximately 150 audience members. Smith principal Tim Fulcher and advisors Ray Torres and Jen Hartenburg introduced 45 eighth-grade Smith Connectors. Bemis and Wattles Elementary were honored as National Blue Ribbon Schools, among 337 chosen nationally, recognized by Secretary Arne Duncan in Washington, D.C.; Jeremey Whan and Joyce Brasington received the certificate alongside retired Wattles principal Dr. Judy Garrett. Resolution 14-117 approved the consent agenda; 14-118 accepted the audited 2014 financial statements presented by Plante Moran audit partner Teresa Pollock for the year ended June 30, 2014; 14-119 appointed Rick West Treasurer for December 2014; 14-120 named West Director and Patricia Orczykowski Alternate Director to the MAISL Joint Risk Management Trust; 14-121 authorized refunding all or part of the 2006 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds dated May 24, 2006, with estimated savings at current rates of $3,356,520; 14-122 rescinded the May 7, 2013 award to Integrated Design Solutions, LLC; 14-123 approved Convergent/Wright & Hunter as Information Technology Architect; and 14-124 awarded a fleet vehicle to Gorno Ford for $28,479.00 from the 2014-2015 General Fund under MiDEAL State Contract Pricing #071B1300005. Every vote was 7-0; the meeting adjourned at 8:20 PM, minutes by Secretary Karl Schmidt. The December 16, 2014 workshop opened at 6:00 PM under Vice-President Miletti with Philippart and Hauff absent, covering Schools of Choice 105 and 105C enrollment projections, 2015 spring assessments and policy review, and adjourned at 9:30 PM.

The Wire Transfers listing totals −$1,962,542.81; the ACH Debits journal listing, whose P-Card lines span 10/26/2014 to 11/28/2014, totals $197,869.60. **Personnel and curriculum.** A probationary contract for the remainder of 2014-2015 was recommended for Karly Didocha, Resource Room Teacher at Troy High School — B.A. Alma College April 1996, M.A. University of Detroit Mercy May 2003 in special education/emotional impairments, Ed.S. Siena Height College Adrian May 2011, Michigan Professional Certificate renewal March 2014, previously Waterford Schools and Southfield Public Schools. Anne Mull, Director of Assessments, Equity and Federal Grants, presented 2015 Spring Assessments. Under Section 105 of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, the district would seat 100 kindergarten and 50 first grade non-resident students from Oakland County for 2015-16, with the same 100 and 50 under Section 105c for contiguous ISDs, and 20 non-resident sixth through eighth graders at Baker Middle School under each.

**Other reports.** The Superintendent Goals Update, the second of the year with the next due in April, covers operational effectiveness (100% usage compliance of eFinance HR, Payroll and Accounts Receivable modules; weekly work order review of privatized preventive maintenance; bi-weekly bond updates with TMP and Barton Malow), achievement (85% completion of early college and career programs and bottom 30% at-risk identification), leadership and strategic planning. The Central Office WIG Scorecard dated 1/8/2015 records weekly agreements of Birmingham 5 or more, Dziatczak 4 or more, Keeling 4 or more, Machesky 5 or more, West 3 or more and Witt 3 or more. The draft communication plan describes School Messenger, the advertiser-supported School Life newspaper, monthly Superintendent podcasts, OneTroy videos, TS-TV and Vimeo, noting Facebook fans increased more than 100% and Twitter followers more than tripled in the past 12 months. Kerry Birmingham, Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives, reported on the TSD Advocacy Initiative. Barton Malow and TMP presented the 2013 Bond Program – Series 1 update: secure entry canopies at Leonard, Wattles, Morse and Hill; Troy High School, Boulan Park and Larson additions completing about December 2015; the Athens LGI renovation in spring 2015; and bid packages BP #8 through BP #13 covering mechanical and electrical upgrades, Hill and Troy Union roofing, conversion of the International Academy East pool to an LGI room, a Schroeder bus loop, and Smith gymnasium and Niles restroom renovations. The meeting closed with a resolution to enter closed session on the Superintendent's Mid-Year Evaluation as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call of Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Schmidt.
